saints.name: St. Onesimus
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The runaway slave of Philemon whom St. Paul begot in his chains and sent back as “no longer a slave, but a brother”…
biography: Onesimus was a slave of Philemon, a Christian of Colossae in Phrygia. Fleeing his master, he came to Rome, where he found the imprisoned Apostle Paul and was converted — 'my child,' Paul calls him, 'Onesimus, whose father I have become in my imprisonment.'

About the year 61 Paul sent him home with Tychicus, bearing the Epistle to Philemon, the tenderest of his letters, pleading that the runaway be received 'no longer as a slave but more than a slave, as a beloved brother.' He is named also in the Epistle to the Colossians as 'one of yourselves.'

Tradition holds that he was freed and served the Church: an Onesimus appears, about the year 107, as bishop of Ephesus in the letters of Ignatius of Antioch. The Roman Martyrology honours him as bishop of Ephesus after Timothy, brought a prisoner to Rome and there stoned to death for the faith of Christ, his body afterwards carried back to the church he had governed.
saints.knownFor: The convert-slave of the Epistle to Philemon.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 16 February
